continuation_reasoning:
iotic resistance arises through natural selection, a cornerstone of evolutionary theory. When antibiotics are introduced, they kill susceptible bacteria, leaving behind resistant strains. These resistant bacteria then reproduce, passing on their resistance traits. Over time, the proportion of resistant bacteria increases in the population.

Overprescription of antibiotics accelerates this process. When antibiotics are used unnecessarily or inappropriately, it exposes more bacteria to these drugs, increasing the chances of resistant strains surviving and proliferating. Additionally, incomplete courses of antibiotics can lead to the survival of partially resistant bacteria, which can then evolve further resistance.

In summary, antibiotic resistance is driven by the selective pressure of antibiotics, which favors the survival and reproduction of resistant bacteria. Overprescription intensifies this selective pressure, speeding up the emergence and spread of resistant strains.
